memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And God said, "Let the water under the sky be gathered to one place, and let dry ground appear." And it was so. God called the dry ground "land," and the gathered waters he called "seas." And God saw that it was good. - Gen 1:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
I've combined these verses, as they form one complete act, God gathering the waters and revealing the land.

Once more God speaks, and creation obeys. The waters gather, the dry ground appears, and "it was so." God sets a boundary for the sea and a place for the land, and each stays where He has appointed it. Even the mighty ocean knows its limits under God's command (Job 38:8-11).

There is real comfort in this. The same God who tells the seas where to stop is the God who rules over the storms and floods of our lives. Nothing is out of control. When circumstances feel like rising waters threatening to overwhelm you, remember, God sets the boundaries, and nothing crosses the line He has drawn without His knowing.

And again God pauses to say it is good. He delights in His work. The solid ground beneath your feet, the seas, the shorelines, all of it came from a good God who takes pleasure in what He makes.

Years later, Jesus would stand in a boat and speak to a raging sea, and it grew calm at His word (Mk 4:39). The One who first set the sea's boundaries is the same One who still speaks peace into our storms. Whatever floods your life today, He remains Lord over it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "rising waters" in your life do you need to entrust to God's control?
2. Do you believe God has set limits even on your hardest circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You command the seas and set their boundaries. Speak Your peace over the storms in my life, and help me rest in Your control. Amen.
